questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I preffered an english speaking country, so it was easier to adapt and communicate as well. This was also my first time going abroad alone. It was also important to me to get on campus housing and intresting courses, that arent restricted for exchange students, so SFU was a great choice.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I made meaningful friendships and really bonded with my friends over the course of just 4 months. It made this all memorable. Also I had the chance to make great connections for my academic career as well, such as MA and PhD students and professor who's work I found interesting.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy since they hosted an online meeting before our arrival. So we got a lot of inromationa about our exchange agreemsnts, things to know about the academics, school structure and spirit. etc.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was very happy to get on campus housing, so on move in day there were many volunteers, students and staff guiding you throughout the day. They were always so helpful when you had questions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Many buildings to choose from. I was in Barbara Rae, which is one of the North Towers. I was very satisified I had an all girls floor, it was peacful and clean. Th eother buildings such as West and East are the newer ones, they are more modern and look nicer, but I am not sure if they have single gender flooring. Also I know that the water pressure for the sink and shower is much better in Barbara Rae compared to East and West, just for information.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Meal plan and it was obiligatory to get for certain buildings because those did not have a full kitchen. The food was quiet nice in the dining hall, lots of things to choose from and they try to change and add new things and listen to the feedback if there is need for improvment.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Do the research so you know which builidng is best for you and your wished, also apply as early as possible.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Simple application site where you applied giving the general information and then your grade average and you had to write a short essay explaining why you are interested in SFU.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Moslty through emails.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was very happy to get all the classes I wished for, so it was based on a priority list that you give them when you apply.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Check things such as requirements, prerequisites and overall level. Also if possible try using
ratemyprofessor.com
to get an idea of how good the proff. for that course is.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was very happy with my courses and found them intresting and also good proffesors.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had some classes where there was a mix of BA and MA students.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It wasy very similar, nothing different in the lecture style but I didnt have as many tutorials compared to UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
BPK142
MATH360
CHEM419
CHEM439

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of them if you are in STEM or interested. BPK142 was about Biomathematics and the professor was really good at explaining and showed interest in his field of work as well.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were many clubs to choose from so cultural ones that focused on cultural values by hosting events, social meetups etc. or other clubs that focused on organizing things with non-profit companies like charity based or blood drives. Different sports were there too so you could just walk in and participate. Also the hiking club.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Badminton, hiking club, SFU Blood, Organ, and Stem Cell Club, dining commitee (to give feedback on the meal plan options)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Do as much in Semptember to October or at least before the weather is only constant rainy days, especially if you want to do certain outdoor activities. Go to Stanley Park, Granville Island, visit a pumpkin patch, go to the Vancouver Aquarium, Botanical Gardens, Gas Town (visit different cafes and gift shops), I reccomend Waffle Land and Shop Makers. Lee's Doughnuts is overrated.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy, I didnt feel that many things were different except the tipping culture. Also some things were different with the public transport than what I am used to at home but it was easy to adjust.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to the Exchange events where we mostly did socialize, they were usually at the beginning of the term. Also if you live on campus you will meet way more people on Move in Day, Dining Hall and the activities that were organized on Welcome week.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really challenging but had to get used to tipping and also the tax is not included on the price for most items.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openess to help from people and the kind attitude.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Start it with an optimistic approach and make the best out of it. Have an open mind and don't let one bad experience ruin the whole exchange.
Remember to socialize and meet people and make good connections, so it doesnt get too lonely.
Experience as much as you can, just go for it because it all goes by so fast, before you know it.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do a good amount of research in good time, so you know how to apply and if SFU is the right choice for you based on your preferences and expectations.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making such good friends that were really hard to say bye to at the end of the exchange experience but great connections that we already want to meet again somewhere in the future.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
Any other comments?
questions.answer: Don't think twice. I was a little unsure in the beginning if I should go on this exchange but I am so glad I made the right decision. Make the most out of it!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
